    Estimate detection probability and occupancy

    Source: R/inv-introduction.R
    inv_detection_prob.Rd

    Fits the constant single-season occupancy model of MacKenzie et al. (2002) by maximum likelihood to repeated presence/absence surveys. It separates the probability that a site is occupied (psi) from the probability of detecting the species on one survey of an occupied site (p), which is essential for surveillance of rare new incursions.

    Usage

    inv_detection_prob(.data, surveys, .by = NULL, confidence = 0.95)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame with one row per site and one column per survey.

    surveys

    <tidy-select> Survey columns holding 1 (detected), 0 (not detected) or NA (not surveyed).

    .by

    <tidy-select> Optional grouping columns, for example region or habitat.

    confidence

    Target confidence used for surveys_needed.

    Value

    A tibble with one row per group: n_sites, n_surveys (maximum per site), naive_occupancy, psi and psi_se, p and p_se, cumulative_p (probability of at least one detection across n_surveys at an occupied site), surveys_needed (surveys required to be confidence sure an undetected species is absent from an occupied site) and log_lik.

    References

    MacKenzie, D. I., Nichols, J. D., Lachman, G. B., Droege, S., Royle, J. A. and Langtimm, C. A. (2002). Estimating site occupancy rates when detection probabilities are less than one. Ecology, 83, 2248-2255.

    Examples

    inv_detection_prob(inv_surveys, surveys = starts_with("visit"))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 10
#>   n_sites n_surveys naive_occupancy   psi psi_se     p   p_se cumulative_p
#>     <int>     <dbl>           <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>        <dbl>
#> 1     150         5           0.327 0.386 0.0483 0.344 0.0377        0.879
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: surveys_needed <dbl>, log_lik <dbl>
inv_detection_prob(inv_surveys, surveys = starts_with("visit"), .by = habitat)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 11
#>   habitat   n_sites n_surveys naive_occupancy   psi psi_se     p   p_se
#>   <chr>       <int>     <dbl>           <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 urban          48         5           0.312 0.349 0.0767 0.416 0.0671
#> 2 grassland      43         5           0.465 0.550 0.0980 0.339 0.0587
#> 3 forest         59         5           0.237 0.316 0.0863 0.263 0.0708
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: cumulative_p <dbl>, surveys_needed <dbl>, log_lik <dbl>
